newsitem.title: POLAND: Ameritech sells stake in Polish firm - papers.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech sells stake in Polish firm - papers.

text.p: Ameritech Corp. has sold its 24.5-percent stake in the Polish cellular telephone firm Centertel SA to the company's two other shareholders, newspapers reported on Wednesday.

Two newspapers, Gazeta Wyborcza and Rzeczpospolita, quoted sources which declined to be named as saying that after the sale Poland's state-owned telecom firm TPSA would have 66 percent in Centertel and France Telecom 34 percent.
Before the sale, sparked by a conflict over power and profit sharing in Centertel, TPSA had 51 percent of shares and France Telecom 24.5 percent.
Centertel spokesman Jacek Kalinowski said that talks on the sale of the Ameritech stake were well advanced but that he did not know whether they were completed.
"Talks are well advanced but I have not received any official information," he told Reuters. TPSA and France Telecom officials were not immediately available for comment.
Newspapers reported that Ameritech, which bought its Centertel shares for $36 million, would now sell it for about $50 million.

The partnership in Centertel, set up in 1991, turned sour last year when TPSA, arguing that its role in the company did not reflect its majority shareholding, began seeking more say in the firm's management and a bigger share in profits.
Earlier this year TPSA blocked Ameritech and France Telecom's plans to seek one of two licences to develop a modern digital GSM system for Centertel, which now operates an older analogue system.
The licences went to two consortia of Polish and foreign companies, which have launched operations to challenge Centertel.
